description: Projection of the 20261027T072436Z saved refresh review. Evidence and verdict are verbatim; unrelated snapshot nodes omitted. Not a compilable design or semantic adjudication. Requirements retain IDs only.

D_BANK_COUNT.reason: The requested controller exposes four logical DDR4 banks.

D_DDR4_PROFILE.reason: The requested 3200 speed selects the DDR4-3200 timing profile.

D_FIFO_ORDERING.reason: FIFO behavior is interpreted as ordered service by request-admission order without row-hit bypass.

D_HOST_TRANSACTION_MODEL.reason: A request/response interface is derived for the requested memory-controller behavior; writes have no response and reads return one captured response.

D_MEMORY_MODEL.reason: A functional banked memory model provides independently verifiable read/write behavior for the controller specification.

D_REFRESH_POLICY.reason: Defines deterministic refresh behavior while preserving FIFO contents and preventing new dispatch after pending refresh becomes visible.

D_RESET_STYLE.reason: The supported lowering convention uses one rising-edge clock, active-low synchronous state reset, reset priority, and suppressed protocol events while reset is asserted.

D_RESPONSE_LATENCY.reason: A committed READ captures pre-edge memory data and presents one response for host sampling at the following rising edge.

A_ADDRESS_MAPPING.statement: The derived host mapping uses txn_bank as the bank index, txn_addr[15:8] as row, and txn_addr[7:0] as column. The functional memory model indexes one DATA_WIDTH-bit word per bank/row/column combination.

A_CLOCK_DURING_RESET.statement: clk continues during reset and rst_n is asserted across at least one rising clk edge when state cancellation is required.

A_HOST_STABILITY.statement: When txn_valid is high and txn_ready is low, the host holds txn_bank, txn_addr, txn_is_write, and txn_wdata stable until admission or reset.

A_RESPONSE_CONSUMPTION.statement: The host samples rsp_rdata when rsp_valid is high at a rising edge. There is no response-ready signal and no response backpressure.

A_TIMING_SCOPE.statement: This specification enforces the explicitly requested DDR4 timing protections tFAW, tRAS, and tRCD, plus refresh interval exclusion tRFC. It does not claim complete JEDEC DDR4 command-timing coverage beyond those documented constraints.

owned_state.deadline: Periodic tREFI deadline referenced to the most recent reset edge.
owned_state.service_state: Committed REF age and validity representing tRFC service exclusion.

handshakes.request: shared.events.refresh_due sets sticky pending state. Pending persists until REF acknowledgment except when simultaneous due retains it.
handshakes.acknowledgment: shared.events.refresh_start is exactly a committed REF command.

refresh.reset: Clear deadline, pending, and service state synchronously. pending and service_busy are low during reset.

update_events.shared.events.refresh_due: Set pending and advance periodic deadline by tREFI.
update_events.shared.events.refresh_start: Start tRFC service and clear pending unless refresh_due also occurs.
update_events.shared.events.refresh_end: End service exclusion while preserving independently accumulated pending state.

refresh.stalls: Deadlines continue while waiting for active completion, bank closure, or service completion. Refresh does not own FIFO requests.

simultaneous_events.due_and_refresh_start: Due wins pending update; REF starts service and another pending refresh remains.
simultaneous_events.due_and_refresh_end: Service ends but pending remains set.

owned_state.active_request: Validity and complete dispatched request retained until final committed READ or WRITE.
owned_state.candidate: Registered non-NOP command proposal and validity.
owned_state.refresh_preparation: Ascending-bank close preparation state after refresh pending becomes visible.

handshakes.dispatch: shared.events.dispatch captures the pre-edge FIFO head only when no active request exists and refresh is neither pending nor in service.
handshakes.candidate: Candidate formation uses registered active ownership and pre-edge bank state. A blocked candidate remains unchanged and has no architectural effect.
handshakes.commit: shared.events.command_commit occurs only for a valid timing-permitted candidate. The committed command is broadcast unchanged.

command_engine.reset: Clear active request, candidate, and refresh-preparation state. Suppress dispatch_ready, candidate_valid, and commit_valid during reset. Invalid command payload is NOP.

update_events.shared.events.dispatch: Capture the complete dispatched request into active ownership. Candidate generation starts only on a later edge.
update_events.shared.events.command_commit: ACT and PRE retain active ownership. Final READ or WRITE retires it. During refresh preparation, PRE advances bank closure and REF completes an acknowledgment.
update_events.every_clock: When no candidate is outstanding, refresh is inactive, and reset is inactive, form the next registered candidate from active ownership, bank state, and refresh preparation.

command_engine.stalls: Candidate and active payload remain stable across timing stalls. No same-edge replacement dispatch follows retirement. Visible refresh pending blocks dispatch.

simultaneous_events.refresh_due_and_final_commit: The final active command may commit using pre-edge refresh state; pending becomes visible afterward.
simultaneous_events.retirement_and_dispatch: Retirement does not permit same-edge replacement dispatch.

owned_state.words: Functional DATA_WIDTH-bit words indexed by bank, row, and column.
owned_state.response_slot: Registered response data and validity with capacity one.

handshakes.commit: Samples shared.events.command_commit. Committed WRITE changes one word; committed READ captures its pre-edge word only when response storage is empty.
handshakes.response: shared.events.response_delivery samples rsp_valid on the edge after READ capture. Validity clears after delivery unless reset applies.

memory.reset: Synchronously zero memory, response validity, and response data. rsp_valid is low during reset.

update_events.shared.events.command_commit: Apply committed WRITE mutation or capture committed READ pre-edge memory data; ignore other opcodes.
update_events.shared.events.response_delivery: Clear response validity after sampled delivery; retain captured data while invalid.

memory.stalls: Blocked commands never mutate memory, capture data, or overwrite response storage. Valid response storage prevents new READ retirement.

simultaneous_events.response_delivery_and_read: Forbidden because READ retirement requires empty pre-edge response storage.
simultaneous_events.response_delivery_and_write: Deliver the old response and apply independent write mutation.

refresh_due.condition: At a rising edge, rst_n is high and the periodic refresh deadline is reached.
refresh_due.effect: Set sticky refresh-pending state. A due event does not discard waiting requests and does not cancel an already active request.

refresh_end.condition: At a rising edge, rst_n is high and the edge is at least tRFC cycles after the committed REF edge.
refresh_end.effect: End refresh command exclusion. A later pending refresh, if any, remains pending.

SYS_REFRESH.statement: The first refresh due edge after reset is E0+tREFI, where E0 is the last rising edge sampled with reset asserted. Later due deadlines advance by tREFI independent of REF commit. Due sets sticky pending state; due events during pending or service coalesce. Once pending is visible before an edge, no new dispatch occurs. Any already active request may finish, then all open banks are closed in ascending bank order before REF commits. REF starts tRFC command exclusion. If refresh_due and REF commit occur on the same edge, pending remains set for a later refresh.

SYS_SIMULTANEOUS_EVENTS.statement: Reset has priority over every other event. Otherwise, admission and dispatch may occur together using pre-edge FIFO contents: dispatch removes the old head and admission appends the sampled new request. refresh_due may coincide with a legal command commit based on pre-edge pending state; the command completes and pending becomes set after the edge. A pending refresh visible before an edge prevents dispatch on that edge. Response delivery and a new READ retirement cannot coincide because retirement requires empty response storage.

execution.verification.V_EXEC_COMMAND_CO.note: Probe candidate signals as the indirect timing-history check. For blocked WRITE cases, retain attempted address/data in an independent memory scoreboard and subsequently issue/read back the affected location to prove no mutation. Observe refresh pending/service state and response outputs to prove blocked proposals produce no refresh or response side effect.

EXEC_RESPONSE_EDGE.statement: A READ committed at edge E captures its pre-edge memory word and makes rsp_valid and rsp_rdata registered outputs after E. The host delivery event occurs when those outputs are sampled at edge E+1. If no reset applies, rsp_valid clears after that delivery edge and rsp_rdata retains its last captured value while rsp_valid is low.

findings.message: The refresh contract owns both the periodic deadline and REF service age, but specifies no every-clock maintenance that advances the deadline toward refresh_due or advances service age toward refresh_end. The only declared refresh updates are on refresh_due, refresh_start, and refresh_end themselves, while those events depend on the deadline/service-age conditions already becoming true. Consequently, the current contracts do not define a realizable progression from the last reset edge to the first due edge, nor from a committed REF to service_busy deassertion at tRFC; refresh may never become pending or service may remain busy indefinitely. Define refresh every-clock state evolution, including initialization from the last reset-sampled edge, deadline comparison/advance, service-age advance and tRFC expiry, and its priority relative to simultaneous due, REF start, refresh end, and reset.

repair_assessments.explanation: The command-commit verification binding now observes refresh pending/service and host response outputs. Its note also requires an independent memory scoreboard and later readback for blocked WRITE attempts, providing a way to distinguish an attempted blocked write from an unintended memory mutation. Candidate probes remain available for indirect timing-history effects.

preservation_assessment.explanation: The repaired command-commit verification bindings preserve the required candidate, bank-state, refresh, response, and readback-scoreboard observability without introducing a contradiction in reset priority, FIFO ownership, command retirement, or response-delivery ordering. The remaining refresh-timebase defect is a current contract incompleteness and is not a regression of the repaired command-commit observability finding.

original_findings.message: The command-commit check claims to verify that blocked or invalid proposals leave all observable architectural state unchanged, and its scenario requires independent observation of timing history, memory, refresh, and response behavior. Its declared observations expose only candidate signals and bank state. In particular, a blocked WRITE cannot be distinguished from an unintended memory mutation without subsequently observing a read response, and refresh or response side effects cannot be checked from the listed observations. Extend this check's bindings and scenario instrumentation to observe refresh and response state and to perform/read back memory-scoreboard checks for blocked-command cases; retain candidate probes as the indirect timing-history check.
